title: Meridian Finance - SOC 2 / ISO 27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood team reviewed SOC 2 and ISO-27001 posture, discussed access to reports and trust center, controls mapping deliverable, RBAC/SSO options, audit log retention, KMS and BYOK, and private/VPC deployment constraints. Agreed next steps include sharing SOC 2 Type II report, controls matrix, and scheduling a follow-up technical deep dive to validate KMS and audit log retention behavior.
next_steps: Alex to send SOC 2 Type II report and controls mapping link (Redwood trust center)
Samir to schedule technical deep dive on KMS/BYOK and audit logs (separate call)
Customer to confirm timeline for procurement and relaxed firewall rules for test bench
action_items: Owner: Alex Park - Send SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) and ISO-27001 controls mapping spreadsheet; Due: 2026-06-17
Owner: Samir Patel - Prepare KMS/BYOK notes + sample terraform for VPC connector; Due: 2026-06-24
Owner: Priya Sharma (Meridian) - Share list of required audit events and retention policy; Due: 2026-06-15
Owner: Tom Nguyen - Provide sample test account details and IP ranges for pilot; Due: 2026-06-18
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Lee (Meridian - Head of Security), Tom Nguyen (Meridian - Cloud Architect), Priya Sharma (Meridian - Compliance), Evan Brooks (Meridian - Dir Eng)

00:00 Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time. i'm alex park from redwood, i'll kick us off. samir will jump in the deep infra bits. quick agenda - SOC two and ISO twenty seven oh one posture, access to our trust center, controls mapping, and then some KMS / audit log Qs. sound good?
00:18 Rachel (Meridian): yeah that's great, alex. we have about 50 minutes, we want to make sure we validate the reports and understand how you map controls to our frameworks, and also the SSO and RBAC story.
00:30 Alex: perfect. quick context - Meridian mentioned you're running regulated finance workloads, correct, and you need SOC two type II plus ISO 27001 evidence for your auditors?
00:40 Rachel: correct. and we also have strict data residency reqs in us-east-1, and we use a customer-managed KMS for some keys.
00:52 Samir (Redwood SE): ok noted, and do you expect to use Redwood Hosted or are you looking at dedicated / private?
01:02 Tom (Meridian): preference is private or VPC option for now. procurement may push for dedicated later but we want the private control plane for auditability.
01:12 Samir: got it. our private deployment supports customer-managed KMS (BYOK) and full audit logging to your cloud logging endpoint, we can instrument syslog or cloudwatch depending on provider. just to flag, some customers mishear that as 'BYOK is alpha' — it's GA for private deployments.
01:30 Priya (Meridian): can you walk through the SOC 2 report access? do we get the whole report or a redacted copy?
01:38 Alex: good q. we provide SOC 2 Type II report via our trust center link — typically it's the full report for customers under NDA / DPA. we'll share a download link and a short controls mapping doc that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks. i'll send access details after this call.
01:52 Rachel: and for ISO 27001, do you have the certificate and statement of applicability?
01:58 Alex: we have an ISO 27001 cert yes and a controls mapping doc; often we provide the cert and a mapping spreadsheet, the soa (statement of applicability) is a bit more controlled, but we can discuss redactions if needed.
02:12 Evan (Meridian): what about audit logs - what events are captured and how long retained? our auditors want 2 years of logs for certain events.
02:20 Samir: default retention depends on deployment: hosted has 90 days, dedicated can be extended, private is customer controlled — we stream logs to your endpoint and retention is whatever your logging infra configures. we do keep immutable audit trails in our control plane for certain admin events for 1 year; we can discuss extensions.
02:40 Tom: ok so for private we'd handle retention, but we also want proof you don't keep decrypted customer content in your control plane, esp for cache keys and KV cache.
02:52 Samir: yes we can provide a controls note — data-in-transit and at-rest are encrypted; for private deployments keys can be customer-managed, and we don't store plaintext models or customer data outside of configured storage. the KV cache is encrypted and bound to the deployment. note: sometimes the transcript mis-reads 'KV' as 'K V' in docs, but it's the key-value cache.
03:12 Rachel: SSO - we use SAML with Okta. how's SAML SSO and RBAC enforced?
03:20 Alex: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is role-based with default roles and you can add custom roles. for private, you can tie it to your IdP and we surface audit events for admin changes.
03:34 Priya: can you provide a list of the roles and the exact audit events tied to RBAC changes? auditors will want that mapping.
03:42 Samir: yes, we'll include a role matrix in the controls mapping doc. sample events include account.create, account.update.role, token.create, token.revoke, model.deploy, model.rollback, and auth.fail events. we'll put the exact event names in the doc 
03:58 Evan: are service logs tamper-evident?
04:02 Samir: for private deployments, logs are pushed to your endpoint — so tamper-evidence comes from your logging stack. for hosted we have immutability controls and tamper detection for audit trails in the control plane. i'll outline specifics in the follow-up.
04:18 Rachel: good. can you also confirm encryption algorithms and FIPS support? our policy mandates AES-256 and FIPS for key management.
04:26 Samir: we use AES-256-GCM at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit. for KMS we integrate with customer-KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and FIPS endpoints are supported depending on provider region. i'll note the exact cipher suites and FIPS configurations in the tech deep dive doc.
04:44 Tom: on data residency — we need processing to stay in us-east-1 for our pilot; can you guarantee that?
04:52 Alex: yes, we can pin routing and deployment to specific regions. for private/VPC we deploy into your VPC subnets in us-east-1. for hosted, we can route requests to region-specific clusters but full data residency guarantees are stronger for private.
05:08 Rachel: any third-party subprocessors? we need a list for our vendor risk team.
05:14 Alex: yes, we maintain a subprocessor list in the trust center; it includes cloud providers and some observability partners. we'll share the latest list and the vendor attestation.
05:24 Priya: more on controls mapping — can you map your SOC 2 controls to our ISO control numbers? we have a template we like.
05:34 Alex: totally, we'll map SOC 2 criteria to ISO 27001 clauses in the spreadsheet; it's a fairly standard crosswalk. i'll attach that.
05:44 Samir: and from the infra side, for the pilot you'll likely want a short lived pilot token and a dedicated test cluster or VPC peering. for private, we can spin up a test stack in your account.
05:58 Tom: that works. what about backups - how long and where are model artifacts backed up?
06:06 Samir: backups for model artifacts are encrypted and located in customer region for private; retention policy is configurable. for hosted we replicate across regions for availability but you can request data residency constraints.
06:20 Rachel: can you show where to find the trust center link?
06:24 Alex: yes link is in our docs — https://trust.redwood-inference.com (we'll provide access). note: sometimes the auto transcript munges urls in the export.
06:36 Priya: regarding certifications - do you have continuous monitoring or SOC 2 re-audits cadence?
06:42 Alex: SOC 2 Type II is annual; penetration testing cadence is annual and we publish a summary. ISO recertification is on schedule and we'll share cert dates.
06:54 Evan: anything in there about supply chain security?
06:58 Samir: we have a vendor management program and secure software development lifecycle; we'll attach the high level. for deeper questions we can include our security engineering lead in the follow-up.
07:12 Rachel: can you confirm breach notification SLAs? our policy requires 72-hour notification to impacted customers.
07:20 Alex: yes we have incident response commitments; for customers with enterprise agreements we put notification SLA in the contract. standard practice is to notify within 72 hours for incidents impacting customer data.
07:30 Tom: about logging formats - will you push structured json events or syslog?
07:36 Samir: we can push structured JSON over HTTPS to a collector or support syslog/Cloud PubSub depending on provider. we'll include sample event schema.
07:48 Priya: auditors ask for control ownership - who owns encryption config?
07:52 Alex: for private deployments encryption config is owned by the customer; for hosted/dedicated Redwood owns the default platform config but provides a controls mapping showing responsibilities (shared responsibility model).
08:06 Rachel: ok let's talk timelines - procurement wants a pilot in July and a security review by August for vendor onboarding. is that feasible?
08:14 Alex: yes, pilot in July is reasonable; i'll coordinate with Samir to scope the pilot resources and we'll follow up with dates.
08:24 Samir: i'll plan a technical deep dive next week to walk KMS and log shipping and include terraform snippets for VPC connector.
08:34 Evan: small ask - can you redact any model detail in the SOC doc? our legal wants to ensure nothing proprietary is exposed.
08:40 Alex: yes we can work with legal on redactions, we often sign a mutual NDA when sharing full reports.
08:48 Priya: for the controls matrix, can you map control owner, control frequency, and evidence location? that's what auditors want.
08:56 Alex: yes that's standard; we'll include a column for evidence and sample artifacts in the mapping doc.
09:06 Rachel: anything else?
09:10 Tom: one more on backup key destruction — if we rotate keys, how is historical data handled?
09:18 Samir: key rotation policies depend on KMS; if you rotate customer keys in BYOK, old keys can be retained for decryption window per your policy; we'll document recommended rotation scripts.
09:30 Alex: ok let's recap next steps - i'll share SOC 2 Type II PDF, ISO cert, controls mapping, subprocessor list, and trust center link. samir will schedule tech deep dive and provide KMS/BYOK notes and sample terraform. priya will send required audit events list. tom will share pilot account details.
09:52 Rachel: sounds good. thanks alex and samir.
09:56 Alex: thanks everyone. we'll target sending the docs by next week.
10:00 [call ends]

Notes about transcript: occasional filler words, some product names are mis-transcribed (e.g., SOC two, ISO twenty seven oh one). timestamps are approximate and the auto-transcription introduced minor spacing errors and url munging. Links to artifacts referenced: https://trust.redwood-inference.com/soc2 (access requires login), controls mapping (internal link will be attached in follow-up), sample terraform snippets to be shared in tech deep dive.
